ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **OpenAI: Astra for Law with GPT-6 Astra:** OpenAI has introduced Astra for Law, a new AI foundation designed specifically for law firms and legal technology companies, integrating its powerful GPT-6 Astra model with legal-specific tools and a vast index of over 230 million legal URLs. This specialized offering significantly enhances the model's performance on legal tasks, demonstrating 54% correctness on private legal research questions compared to 38.7% for the general GPT-6 Astra with web search. Legal professionals can now leverage a highly specialized AI for in-depth legal research and analysis, drastically speeding up document drafting and complex legal query resolution, potentially replacing extensive manual database searches.

• **Google DeepMind: Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking:** Google DeepMind formally confirmed the availability of Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking via the Gemini API, Google Workspace, and the Gemini app on September 17, 2026. These are Google's most advanced live dialogue models, with 3.8 Live optimized for conversational intelligence, visual grounding, and cost efficiency, while 3.8 Live Extended Thinking focuses on high-complexity tasks, enabling simultaneous reasoning and speaking for fluid multi-step interactions. Developers can now build more intuitive and intelligent voice agents capable of handling complex reasoning and real-time visual context without interrupting conversations, allowing for seamless hands-free task execution across applications.

• **Google: AI Agent Control for Google Home:** Google has released early access to its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, allowing various AI agents, including Claude and ChatGPT, to securely control Google Home devices and access event history since September 16, 2026. This update integrates general-purpose AI models directly into the smart home ecosystem, extending AI capabilities to physical device control beyond previously limited or custom integrations. Users can now issue complex natural language commands to their preferred AI assistant to manage smart home devices, such as "Dim the living room lights and set the thermostat to 72 degrees when I leave the house."

• **Anthropic: Integrated Claude Chat and Cowork Experience:** Anthropic rolled out an update to Claude on September 17, 2026, which enables seamless routing of requests among chat, Cowork, Artifacts, and Design modes without requiring a manual mode switch. This streamlines the user experience by allowing for integrated workflows across different functionalities, unlike prior versions that often necessitated fragmented task management between modes. A knowledge worker can now transition effortlessly from a brainstorming chat to collaborative document editing in Cowork, then to generating a presentation in Design, and export it as a PDF or PowerPoint, all within Claude's unified interface.

Why it matters: The AI landscape is rapidly shifting towards highly specialized and deeply integrated agentic capabilities, enabling more fluid human-AI interaction and automating complex, multi-application workflows.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026:** On September 18, 2026, President Trump signed this legislation into law, expanding Washington's authority to impose economic pressure on Russia and Iran. The act targets Russia's energy and defense industries, including its "shadow fleet" of tankers used to evade sanctions, and authorizes additional measures affecting Iran. It also grants the President power to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying Russian energy or facilitating sanctions evasion. Previously, Russia sanctions were existing, but this law significantly broadens their scope and introduces new tariff powers for the executive branch. This action is expected to increase geopolitical tensions and could lead to significant shifts in global energy markets and trade relationships.

• **SEC "Innovation Exemption" for Tokenized NMS Stock:** On September 17, 2026, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) issued two five-year, conditional exemptions to facilitate the permissioned trading of "Tokenized National Market System (NMS) Stock" through automated market makers (AMMs) and liquidity pools. This relief includes an exemption from the definition of "exchange" for Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) and an exemption from the definition of "dealer" for certain liquidity providers, subject to several conditions. The exemption is effective immediately. This provides a temporary regulatory pathway for the trading of tokenized securities, potentially boosting innovation and investment in blockchain-based financial markets in the US.

• **FTC Action Against Multilevel Marketing Operator Amway:** On September 17, 2026, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the state of Washington announced a proposed order requiring Amway Corp. and two affiliates (World Wide Group, L.L.C. and Leadership Team Development Inc.) to pay $225 million. This resolves allegations of unfair and deceptive tactics in recruiting members to its direct selling and multilevel marketing opportunity, marking the largest monetary recovery ever collected from an MLM in an FTC action. The order mandates changes, including requiring independent business owners (IBOs) to sell at least 70% of products purchased from Amway each month and substantially reducing recruiter compensation if recruited IBOs buy products but do not resell them. This action signals a strong enforcement stance by the FTC against alleged deceptive practices in the multilevel marketing industry.

• **US Sanctions on Cuban Entities:** On September 17, 2026, the United States imposed sanctions on 11 Cuban entities related to nickel reserves and military enterprises. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio specified that four state-run enterprises related to nickel reserves, four military enterprises dedicated to research and development (including for weapons systems), and three military officials were sanctioned. This action targets a system that the US claims enriches the elite and harms ordinary Cubans. This increases economic pressure on Cuba, potentially impacting sectors tied to nickel production and military-affiliated industries.

• **FTC Settlement with FleetCor for Unauthorized Fees:** On September 17, 2026, FleetCor and its CEO agreed to pay $100 million to settle a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) administrative action. The FTC alleged that FleetCor charged small businesses undisclosed and unauthorized fees for fuel cards, despite falsely promising savings. The settlement funds will provide redress to harmed customers, and the order prohibits FleetCor from billing customers without express informed consent, hiding material information behind hyperlinks, and making deceptive claims about its fuel cards. This substantial settlement underscores the FTC's enforcement against deceptive billing practices and provides restitution to affected small businesses.

Why it matters: The enactment of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 marks a significant escalation in US foreign policy, granting the executive branch expanded powers for economic pressure through sanctions and tariffs with broad geopolitical and economic implications.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **European Parliament approval of legislative package to boost Europe's defence readiness:** Previously, national permit-granting processes for defence projects lacked harmonisation and could be lengthy. Now, a new EU-wide default period for permit decisions on defence projects (e.g., new factories or expansions) is set at 42 working days from the acknowledgement of a complete application. National authorities may extend this twice by up to 60 days in exceptional circumstances, capping the total duration at 102 working days. If no decision is made by the deadline, tacit approval applies. The new rules also simplify intra-EU transfers of defence-related products by introducing a new general transfer licence, which Member States are required to publish. Additionally, EU countries can now apply specific exemptions to EU environmental and chemical regulations for justified defence interests. This package significantly streamlines and accelerates defence investments and cross-border operations for defence companies across the EU. It is particularly relevant for businesses and investors in the defence sector, including those in Portugal, by reducing administrative bottlenecks and fostering quicker project realisation.

• **Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1092 supplementing MiFID II with regulatory technical standards for an EU code of conduct for issuer-sponsored research:** Previously, the EU lacked a harmonised code of conduct for investment research directly commissioned and paid for by the issuer of the financial instrument. This new Delegated Regulation establishes binding regulatory technical standards for an EU-wide code of conduct, setting out requirements to ensure objectivity, prevent conflicts of interest, and maintain the integrity of such research. It mandates specific organisational requirements for investment firms involved in issuer-sponsored research, including disclosure obligations and measures to manage potential biases. This directly affects financial market participants, particularly investment firms, banks, and issuers, by imposing new compliance obligations to ensure the independence and transparency of issuer-sponsored research. Portuguese investment firms and companies issuing financial instruments will need to adhere to these new standards to avoid regulatory penalties and maintain market trust.

• **Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2102 amending the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) regarding the list of relevant commodities and products:** Previously, the EUDR (Regulation (EU) 2023/1115) required operators and traders to conduct due diligence for a specified list of commodities (e.g., cattle, cocoa, coffee, palm oil, soy, wood) to ensure they are deforestation-free. This new Delegated Regulation, published in the Official Journal, amends that list by specifically adding soluble coffee, certain palm oil derivatives, and frozen cattle tongues as covered products. These newly added products will become subject to the EUDR's due diligence requirements from December 30, 2027. The amendment also enhances the functioning of the EUDR's Information System to support compliance. This expands the scope of the EUDR, directly impacting businesses in sectors dealing with these newly added commodities. Operators and traders, including those in Portugal, importing, exporting, or placing these products on the EU market, must update their supply chain monitoring and due diligence systems to comply with the deforestation-free requirements by the December 2027 deadline.

Why it matters: This week saw significant progress in strengthening the EU's strategic autonomy through accelerated defence investment approvals and enhanced supply chain controls for critical commodities, alongside steps to improve financial market transparency.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **Alterações à Lei da Imigração (Lei n.º 62/2026):** Esta lei, publicada a 10 de setembro de 2026 e em vigor desde 11 de setembro, modifica significativamente o regime jurídico de entrada, permanência, saída e afastamento de estrangeiros do território nacional. **Anteriormente:** Era possível obter um título de residência sem visto prévio através de mecanismos como a frequência de cursos profissionalizantes ou por ter um filho menor em Portugal. O prazo máximo de detenção administrativa para estrangeiros sem ter cometido um crime era de 60 dias, e a proteção contra o afastamento com base em filhos menores não exigia um período mínimo de residência. **Agora:** Acaba com as últimas vias de regularização sem visto prévio para quem já se encontra em território nacional. As "Notificações de Abandono Voluntário" são substituídas por "deveres de abandono", implicando que a não conformidade pode levar diretamente à detenção e deportação. O período máximo de detenção aumenta de 60 dias para 6 meses, prorrogável até um total de 12 meses. A proteção contra o afastamento de estrangeiros com filhos menores em Portugal passa a exigir 5 anos de residência no país. Foi ainda estabelecido um prazo de 90 dias, prorrogável por mais 30, para a decisão de pedidos de autorização de residência. O impacto prático é um endurecimento das condições para a regularização de cidadãos estrangeiros em Portugal, tornando mais difícil a obtenção de estatuto legal para quem entra sem visto adequado.

• **Redução do IRS e Suplemento Extraordinário de Pensão (Medidas Aprovadas em Conselho de Ministros):** O Conselho de Ministros de 17 de setembro de 2026 aprovou um conjunto de medidas fiscais e de apoio social. **Anteriormente:** As taxas de Imposto sobre o Rendimento das Pessoas Singulares (IRS) para os primeiros seis escalões eram mais elevadas do que as agora aprovadas, e não existia um suplemento extraordinário de pensão automático para baixos rendimentos. **Agora:** Foi aprovada uma Proposta de Lei para reduzir as taxas de IRS entre 0,3 e 0,5 pontos percentuais até ao 6.º escalão de rendimento coletável, com efeitos nos rendimentos de 2026. Esta redução será sentida já em novembro através de alterações na retenção na fonte. Adicionalmente, foi aprovado um Decreto-Lei que concede um suplemento extraordinário de pensão, com valores entre €100 e €200, a pensionistas com rendimentos até €1611,39, a ser pago automaticamente e de uma só vez em dezembro de 2026. O impacto prático é um aumento do rendimento disponível para a maioria das famílias portuguesas e um reforço do poder de compra para os pensionistas com rendimentos mais baixos.

• **Alterações ao Código dos Contratos Públicos (Decreto-Lei n.º 177/2026):** Este Decreto-Lei, publicado a 4 de setembro de 2026 e que entra em vigor a 1 de outubro de 2026, altera e republica o Código dos Contratos Públicos (CCP) para o simplificar, clarificar e agilizar. **Anteriormente:** Os limiares para a adoção dos procedimentos de consulta prévia e ajuste direto eram significativamente mais baixos. Por exemplo, para empreitadas de obras públicas, o limite da consulta prévia era de €150.000 e do ajuste direto era de €30.000. **Agora:** Os limiares para a consulta prévia sobem de €150.000 para €1.000.000 em empreitadas de obras públicas, e de €75.000 para €130.000 nos contratos de locação/aquisição de bens móveis e serviços. Para o ajuste direto, os limiares aumentam de €30.000 para €150.000 em obras públicas, e de €20.000 para €75.000 em bens e serviços. O diploma também consagra a integração digital na contratação pública, incluindo o reconhecimento da possibilidade de utilização de sistemas de inteligência artificial. O impacto prático é uma maior celeridade e desburocratização nos processos de contratação pública, o que beneficia as empresas que participam em concursos.

• **Abertura de Pedidos de Restituição de IVA na Autoconstrução (Decreto-Lei n.º 97/2026):** No âmbito das medidas fiscais para a habitação, uma disposição do Decreto-Lei n.º 97/2026, publicado a 20 de maio de 2026, torna-se operacional a 1 de outubro de 2026. **Anteriormente:** O regime de restituição parcial do Imposto sobre o Valor Acrescentado (IVA) suportado em empreitadas de construção de imóveis para habitação própria e permanente ainda não estava disponível para a submissão de pedidos. **Agora:** A partir de 1 de outubro de 2026, abre o período para apresentação dos pedidos de restituição parcial do IVA para particulares que construam a sua habitação própria e permanente, referentes aos três primeiros trimestres de 2026. O impacto prático é a possibilidade de os cidadãos que constroem a sua casa recuperarem parte do IVA pago, o que pode aliviar significativamente os custos de construção.

Why it matters: As novas regras de imigração e as alterações nos contratos públicos representam mudanças estruturais significativas no acesso à residência e na dinâmica empresarial, enquanto as medidas fiscais e de apoio à habitação oferecem alívio direto a famílias e construtores.

general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **US-China Trade Pact:** US Trade Representative Katherine Tai and Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao signed the "2026 Pacific Stability Pact" in Singapore on September 18. The treaty eliminates tariffs on 45% of critical minerals and establishes a joint AI safety oversight board to coordinate global chip export controls. The S&P 500 rose 1.2% in overnight trading as technology stocks responded to the reduction in supply chain risk. This agreement stabilizes the global semiconductor market and lowers immediate inflationary pressures on consumer electronics. Financial Times

• **Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Lebanese Prime Minister Najib Mikati ratified a formal ceasefire agreement on September 18, mediated by the UN and the United States. The deal mandates a 10-kilometer buffer zone on both sides of the Blue Line and the deployment of 5,000 additional UNIFIL peacekeepers to monitor the border. Military operations in Southern Lebanon ceased at 00:00 GMT on September 19. This prevents a full-scale regional escalation that would have disrupted Mediterranean shipping lanes and oil prices. Reuters

• **ITER Fusion Milestone:** The ITER organization in Saint-Paul-lez-Durance, France, announced on September 18 that its latest plasma shot maintained a stable burn for 1,000 seconds, producing 500 megawatts of thermal power. This is the first time a fusion reactor has exceeded the energy break-even point by a factor of ten for a sustained duration. Three G7 governments announced an immediate $15 billion increase in funding for commercial fusion pilot plants following the result. This marks the shift of nuclear fusion from an experimental physics project to a viable path for global carbon-free baseload power. BBC

• **European Central Bank (ECB):** ECB President Christine Lagarde announced on September 18 that the "Digital Euro" will enter its full public rollout phase on January 1, 2027. The system allows individuals to hold up to €3,000 in digital wallets directly with the central bank to ensure financial stability during systemic crises. Major European commercial banks saw a 3% dip in stock prices due to fears of deposit flight from private accounts to the ECB. This accelerates the global transition toward Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) and challenges the dominance of private payment rails. Deutsche Welle

Why it matters: Today's events signal a synchronized global move toward stabilization through high-level diplomacy and the transition to next-generation financial and energy infrastructures.
